about.title: Fortuna Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Falls happen fast, often on a wet grocery store floor, a cracked sidewalk near Main Street, or a poorly lit stairwell in a Rohnerville Road apartment complex. What happens in the minutes and hours afterward can matter a great deal to a premises liability claim. Under California law, a property owner or business generally has to have known, or reasonably should have known, about a hazard before they can be held responsible for not fixing or warning about it. That's why documenting the scene, getting names of witnesses, and asking about surveillance footage before it's deleted can be so important. We understand how these local claims are built and reviewed on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to find out where you stand.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a Fortuna Premises Case

items.title: Proving Notice
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard before the fall. We can help gather maintenance logs, inspection records, and prior complaint history to build that case.

items.title: Preserving Video Before It's Gone
items.desc: Many stores and apartment complexes overwrite surveillance footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of that footage can make a real difference in a claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Bar Recovery
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for the fall, you may still recover a reduced amount. We can help present the facts in context rather than let partial blame end the conversation.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Fortuna?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, like a city building or school, that window is much shorter and a claim notice may need to be filed within months. It's worth talking to us early so you don't lose the option.

items.question: What if I fell on Main Street or another business corridor in Fortuna and no one saw it happen?
items.answer: Lack of witnesses doesn't automatically end a claim. Photos of the hazard, your own written account soon after the fall, and any nearby business surveillance cameras can all help establish what happened and whether the property owner had notice of the condition.

items.question: Will I have to pay anything upfront to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. Our consultations are free, and we typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless we recover money for you. There's no cost or obligation just to have a conversation about your situation.
